newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Wolters K buys French Groupe Liaisons.
newsitem.headline: Wolters K buys French Groupe Liaisons.

text.p: Dutch publisher Wolters Kluwer NV said on Monday it had acquired all shares of French professional publisher Groupe Liaisons Investissements.
The Dutch group said last week it was in talks with Groupe Liaisons about a possible takeover of the French firm.

Groupe Liaisons has about 400 employees and posts annual turnover of 135 million guilders. The company specialises in publications on social and fiscal subjects, as well as in transport and pharmacology publishing.
Wolters Kluwer said the takeover, of which no financial details were disclosed, would raise turnover of its French subsidiary Wolters Kluwer France to about 350 million guilders per year.
"The acquisition will give both Groupe Liaisons and the French Wolters Kluwer units better opportunities to market electronic (publishing) products," the Dutch firm added.

Business and legal publisher Wolters Kluwer is active in 22 countries and has about 14,000 employees. The group expects 1996 turnover of about 4.2 billion guilders compared with 2.94 billion guilders in 1995.

The group said earlier turnover would be boosted this year by its recent takeover of U.S. tax and legal publisher CCH and predicted in August that its 1996 full-year net profit per share would grow by five percent to 7.00 guilders.
